answer.evidence: The crossbeam is the main body. Rows 0-5 form a tan top band with highlight rows 1-2 and 4 and rivets. Row 5 is a darker front-edge line, and rows 6-8 form a darkening eave shadow and front strip above the opening. Below it, the posts and the gate leaves (rows 9-29) give a front face of about 23 rows. The posts show only a 1-2 row highlight at their heads (rows 9-10) and are otherwise vertical faces with a darker right strip, so they have no real top surface. The leaves are drawn as vertical corrugated panels. The beam still gives the main body a top of 6 rows with an edge line and shadow, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small piece, about 1.5 tiles wide. It has 14 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 0% near-flat coverage like both references. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines carry a tint: dark brown beside the beam and posts, dark blue-grey beside the corrugated leaves. They are not a uniform black sticker line. The crossbeam shows a lit top edge and a darker underside. The gate leaves show corrugation stripes with alternating light and dark bands, and the post heads have their own highlights. Each material ramp has about 3-4 steps, fewer than the references' 5-6, and the total of 18 colours is low. The measured per-tile richness matches or exceeds the references, though, and no large flat areas appear, so a careful artist would accept it next to the references. Reading the details at this size is hard, so the pass is moderately confident.
